findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body: Calling the function returned by `attach` now leaves `handler` registered. Subsequent messages still invoke a supposedly detached handler, while repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners and duplicate processing. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` to preserve the cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
For every attached socket, invoking the returned cancellation function leaves the `"message"` listener active. Any later message still calls the supposedly detached handler, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and memory indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
For any EventEmitter-style socket, calling the function returned by `attach` no longer removes the message handler. Subsequent messages still invoke stale handlers, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and leak resources.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
Calling the disposer no longer revokes the message handler. If a socket remains open or is reused after logout, authorization changes, or subscription teardown, subsequent untrusted messages still reach the stale handler and can execute logic under the prior session context.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
The returned cleanup function no longer detaches `handler`. With a long-lived socket and repeated attach/dispose cycles, listeners and captured state accumulate indefinitely, causing duplicate message processing, memory growth, and eventually EventEmitter listener warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
